sections.title: Fraud tally · Why there is no single "grand total" of fraud
notes: The five categories below measure different things, and they overlap. Adding them together would double count.
Method used here: the tally keeps separate running totals by tier and never sums across tiers.

Tier 1 (measured error, agency-estimated): improper payments, about $3 trillion cumulative from FY2003 to FY2025 (GAO). The OMB dataset sum for FY2004–FY2025 is $2,984.0B (the yearly rows below, each rounded to $0.1B, add up to $2,983.9B). The FY2025 figure is $186B.

Tier 2 (estimated fraud): GAO puts fraud at $233B–$521B per year (based on FY2018–2022 data). Estimated pandemic fraud: SBA OIG found more than $200B potentially fraudulent in PPP and EIDL, and GAO estimates $100B–$135B in UI. Those two cover different programs, so the combined pandemic figure is about $300B–$335B, estimated or potential, not adjudicated.
Tier 3 (enforcement outcomes): FY2025 DOJ False Claims Act recoveries were $6.8B. CIGIE reported FY2025 investigative receivables and recoveries of $20.6B. These two overlap, so they are not added.
Tier 4 (claims): DOGE claimed $215B. GAO could not verify most of it.

sections.title: Fraud tally · 6. DOGE savings claims versus the GAO audit
notes: DOGE's website claimed about $215B in savings (unaudited). Its itemized "Wall of Receipts" totaled $110.34B: contracts $61.02B, grants $49.21B, leases $113M.

Contracts: only 27.5% ($16.8B) of claimed contract savings followed DOGE's own stated method. $27.4B was claimed on contracts where no termination action was taken. Examples: a DHA contract claimed at $1.7B saved had no action taken, and an Air Force BIM contract was claimed at $4B against a $3.75B value reduction.
Grants: GAO could not verify 96% ($47.32B) of claimed grant savings.
Leases: DOGE claimed $113M, but its own entries sum to $53.5M, and GAO calculated $31.8M. That is an $81.1M overstatement. 108 of the leases were already being terminated before DOGE existed.
The DOGE temporary organization ended July 4, 2026. Its website was last updated Jan 1, 2026.

Verdict on the headline DOGE savings figure: Disproven as stated. GAO found that the itemized claims were not supported at the amounts claimed. Some real savings exist (at least $16.8B in contract savings computed on DOGE's method), but no audited total is available.
sections.label: Verified by SwampForce

sections.title: Omar · Why the status is Unresolved
notes: No court, prosecutor, agency, or congressional ethics body has published a finding that Elmi is Omar's brother or that the marriage was fraudulent. No charge, indictment, civil denaturalization complaint, or removal case has been filed. In 2026, senior officials said an investigation is open: VP Vance said DOJ is looking at it (May 19), and border czar Homan said HSI/ICE is investigating (Sept. 13). DHS Secretary Mullin has said publicly "we know" she married her brother, but he has produced no document supporting that, and DHS says it does not comment on ongoing investigations. An open investigation is not a finding. Until a charging document, court ruling, or official report is published, the claim cannot be labeled Proven. It also cannot be labeled Disproven, because no official body has cleared it either. Public records have not established the relationship one way or the other.

sections.title: COVID & border · 3. Official assessments of COVID-19 origin
notes: Verdict on "COVID came from a lab leak": Unresolved (no official finding). U.S. intelligence agencies remain split. FBI, DOE and CIA lean toward a lab origin with low to moderate confidence; the NIC and four agencies lean toward natural origin. No agency claims high confidence. The House majority and the current administration say a lab origin is likely, the House minority and WHO SAGO disagree or call the question open, and no court or adjudicative finding exists. Evidence from the June 2026 ODNI release was reported by independent reviewers (Lawfare, CNN, June 2026, leads only) not to establish causation. The one point of broad official agreement: the virus was not developed as a biological weapon (ODNI 2021 and 2023).

accountability-1.title: Improper payments (OMB/agency estimates)
lines: What it measures: Payments that should not have been made, were the wrong amount, or could not be documented ("unknown")
Is it fraud?: Not all fraud. This includes underpayments, paperwork and documentation errors, and eligibility errors. Agencies do not break out the fraud share.

accountability-2.title: GAO fraud estimate
lines: What it measures: A statistical estimate of direct annual losses to fraud
Is it fraud?: Estimated fraud. It partly overlaps improper payments and excludes revenue (tax) fraud.

accountability-3.title: IG questioned costs / funds put to better use
lines: Is it fraud?: Not losses. These amounts may never be disallowed or realized.

accountability-4.title: IG investigative recoveries / DOJ False Claims Act
lines: What it measures: Money ordered or recovered through enforcement
Is it fraud?: Documented enforcement outcomes. They overlap each other, because OIG investigations feed DOJ cases.

accountability-5.title: DOGE savings
lines: Is it fraud?: Not a fraud measure. GAO found the claims largely unverifiable (see below).

accountability-94.title: Documented in charging documents or DOJ releases (Proven that the allegation was made in a court filing; proven as fact only…
lines: Documented in charging documents or DOJ releases (Proven that the allegation was made in a court filing; proven as fact only where a conviction covers it)

Kenya transfers (FOF, "Empire" group). The USAO release on Sept 4, 2025 says Abdiaziz Farah (convicted, sentenced to 28 years) "sent millions of dollars in fraud proceeds abroad." Among other things, his brother in Kenya said he had received "$1,287,000" in the days before Dec 27, 2021. The release describes a $300,000 transfer labeled "family support," an apartment building in Nairobi, and land in Mandera, Kenya. The brother, Ahmednaji Sheikh, was charged with conspiracy to commit international money laundering (allegation): irs.gov
EIDBI. Abdinajib Yussuf allegedly "sent more than $200,000 in fraud proceeds to Kenya" (USAO, Dec 18, 2025, IRS-CI mirror above).

HSS. Asad Adow allegedly used proceeds "to invest in real estate in Kenya" (USAO, Sept 18, 2025). Pristine Health defendants allegedly spent proceeds on travel to London, Sydney, Dubai, Istanbul, and Saudi Arabia (USAO, Dec 18, 2025).
more: Treasury, official statements. On Jan 9, 2026, FinCEN issued four notices of investigation to Minnesota money services businesses, a Geographic Targeting Order (reports on transfers of $3,000 or more to beneficiaries outside the U.S. from banks and transmitters in Hennepin and Ramsey counties), and an alert on child-nutrition fraud. Treasury said law enforcement "has limited insight into the persons located abroad who receive the proceeds": home.treasury.gov; GTO: federalregister.gov. The GTO was renewed Aug 7, 2026, with Treasury saying "a portion of which has been laundered overseas." Neither release names Somalia or al-Shabaab: home.treasury.gov; federalregister.gov

No terrorism charges. No defendant in these fraud cases has been charged under 18 U.S.C. 2339B (material support to a designated FTO) or 18 U.S.C. 2339C (terrorism financing), based on every DOJ release reviewed.

Earlier state record. Minnesota's Legislative Auditor (March 2019) was "unable to substantiate the allegation that individuals in Minnesota sent CCAP fraud money to a foreign country where a terrorist organization obtained and used it": lrl.mn.gov
